    The command gradlew assembleRelease is used to build a release-ready version of an Android application using the Gradle Wrapper. Unlike debug builds, this task compiles your code into an APK (Android Package) intended for end-users and distribution. 
    Key Functions 
    • Builds APKs: It assembles all release variants of your project, creating a fully functional build. 
    • Production Readiness: While it produces a release APK, the file must be signed with a private key and optimized (aligned) before it can be uploaded to the Google Play Store. 
    • No Automatic Install: This command only generates the build files; it does not automatically install the app on a connected device (use gradlew installRelease for that). 
    How to Run It 
    Navigate to your project's root (or the android folder in React Native) and run: 
    • Mac/Linux: ./gradlew assembleRelease
    • Windows: gradlew.bat assembleRelease 
    Output Location 
    Once the build completes successfully, you can typically find the resulting APK file at:
    app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk 
    Usage Tips 
    • Cleaning the Build: If you encounter errors or the APK isn't updating, run ./gradlew clean first to delete old build artifacts.
    • Flavors: If your project uses product flavors (e.g., "dev" or "prod"), the command changes to ./gradlew assemble[FlavourName]Release.
    • Specific Modules: To build only the main app module rather than every module in the project, use ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease.
